description: Negative fixture. Must fail pleading QA. It mislabels this arrest-sealing route as an expungement and a dismissal, names a judge and a prosecutor position that no source supplies, and asserts a fee and a completed service that no source states.

caseData.judgeAddress: 1 Synthetic Courthouse Plaza, Sample City, CA 90000

chargeData.chargeDescription: Arrest record for the offense charged in the diverted case
chargeData.disposition: Successful completion of superior court drug diversion under PC 1000.5

eligibilityData.eligibilityBasisLabel: Expungement and dismissal of the case after diversion under Cal. Penal Code § 851.90
eligibilityData.waitingPeriodText: Eligible immediately after the standard 30-day waiting period
additionalFacts: The set-aside is granted as a matter of right once diversion is complete.
The $120 filing fee has been paid to the clerk.
The prosecuting attorney does not oppose this request.
Service on the prosecuting attorney has been completed.

expectFailure.primaryRule: pleading-qa.ts prohibited-vocabulary rule (HARD): the output text contains the prohibited terms "expungement", "dismissal" and "set-aside" for an arrest-sealing track, which the registry scope restriction forbids — "This is arrest sealing. Do not describe it as dismissal, set-aside or expungement."
additionalReasons: Protected fields are populated: judgeName, judgeAddress, judicialDistrict/department, and OTN are supplied although no source names a judge, a court address, a department, or an OTN for this route (counsel flag cf-07).
Prosecutor position is asserted ("does not oppose"), which is an outside-party act that is never prefilled; relief is discretionary (counsel flag cf-08).
A filing fee amount is asserted although the source review states no filing fee for this route (counsel flag cf-04).
Completed service is asserted although no source states that service occurred and no separate service rule beyond notice to all parties is recorded (counsel flag cf-06).

A "standard 30-day waiting period" is asserted; the registry records the waiting-period duration as "None stated", and the only 30-day period in the source is the court's own post-order forwarding duty under § 851.92.
An arresting agency is named although no source names one.
